correctness.rationale: Exact sink-indicator edge constraints yield the means, facet variances and adjacent covariance. Adjacent independence in dimensions two and three follows respectively from disjoint edges and a one-edge conditional automorphism. The five event types have exactly counted intensities; local dependency bounds satisfy b1 <= (21/2)(d+1)2^-d, b2 <= 2b1, b3=0, giving ordinary TV <=63(d+1)2^-d by Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon Theorem 2. The full Q2 and Q3 orientation spaces and the independently represented exact indicator pairs/atom neighborhoods are verified by checker.py. No finite test is used as a proof of the asymptotic assertion.

value.rationale: Induced-facet sinks are canonical observables of oriented cubes. Their shared codimension-two ridge creates a nonvanishing common-shock dependence parameter 1/4 even as the individual vertex sink probabilities vanish, and the exact transition from independence at d<=3 to positive covariance at d>=4 identifies a sharp, motivated structural boundary. The quantitative bivariate law is usable for simultaneous facet sink-absence probabilities and face-level orientation statistics.
